transcript.content: Hello, welcome in. I'm Dr. Smith. To start off, can you tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Thanks, Dr. Smith. Um… I guess the main thing is that I’ve been having a harder time than I’d like to admit with work that takes sustained concentration. Like, monthly reports or planning a multi-site health event — anything where I have to sit down and really use my brain for a while — it feels like I hit a wall. I keep putting it off, even when I know it’s important.

I’m still getting things done, mostly, but it’s been stressful and I don’t love that I’m struggling with it. Does that make sense?
Thinking back, have you struggled with sustaining focus like this since you were a kid or in school, or is this something that started more recently in your life?

I think it goes back pretty far, yeah. I mean, I did okay in school overall, so I don’t want to make it sound like I was a disaster or anything, but even in elementary school my teachers would tell my parents I was bright, just… kind of always off in my own head.

I’d lose worksheets, forget to turn in homework, that kind of thing. My mom actually had to check my backpack every night for a while, otherwise things just wouldn’t make it from my bag to the teacher. So… yes, I guess it’s not brand new. Is that the kind of thing you mean?
Outside of work tasks, do you notice similar difficulties with focus, organization, or forgetfulness in other areas of your life—like at home, in relationships, or managing daily errands?

Yeah… a bit. I mean, I try to keep systems so it doesn’t become a big problem, but things still slip through sometimes.

Like I’ve forgotten to return calls from volunteers, or I’ll miss small errands connected to events that I really did mean to do. And, um… once or twice I’ve had to apologize because a community meeting completely slipped my mind until someone texted me.

It’s embarrassing, honestly. I don’t think I’m careless, but it probably comes across that way sometimes. Is that the sort of thing you’re asking about?
Do you often feel restless or fidgety, have trouble sitting still, or find yourself acting or speaking impulsively—like interrupting others or blurting things out—more than most people your age?

Not so much the physically restless part, I don’t think. I can sit through meetings, mostly.

I do notice… and this is a little embarrassing… I can talk too much sometimes, especially if I’m nervous that I’ve messed something up. Like if I made a scheduling mistake, I’ll start over-explaining it and just keep going, even when the other person probably already understands. I’m trying to show I wasn’t being careless, I guess.

I don’t know if that counts as impulsive exactly, but it’s something I’ve noticed.
Do you often find yourself interrupting other people mid-conversation or finishing their sentences before they’re done, even when you don’t mean to?

I don’t think that’s a big thing for me, no. I mean, I’m sure I’ve done it here and there like anyone does, especially if I’m trying to show I’m following, but I wouldn’t say I’m constantly cutting people off or finishing their sentences.

If anything, I’m usually trying pretty hard not to come across that way. Does that answer it?
Do you often feel an inner sense of restlessness—like your mind or body is 'on the go'—or find it hard to relax during downtime, even if you're not visibly fidgety?

I’m not sure I’d describe it as being “on the go,” exactly. I can relax sometimes, or at least I think I can.

My mind does keep circling things now and then, especially if I’m worried I forgot something, but I don’t know if that’s the same kind of restlessness you mean. I’m not usually pacing around or anything like that. Maybe I’d say it’s more mental checking than restlessness, if that makes sense.
Do you often find it hard to wait your turn—like in lines or during conversations—or do you tend to make decisions quickly without fully thinking them through?

I don’t think waiting my turn is a major issue for me. Lines are annoying, like for anybody, but I’m not usually the person trying to jump ahead or anything.

With decisions… I try to be pretty careful, especially at work. I might decide quickly on smaller things just to keep things moving, but I wouldn’t say I’m reckless. At least, I don’t think so. If there’s a specific kind of decision you mean, I can try to think about that more.
Sorry, I may have missed the next question. Could you say that again?
Thinking back to when you were a child, were you often described as overly energetic, unable to stay seated, or constantly on the move, more than other kids your age?

I’m honestly not sure. I don’t remember being described that way, at least not clearly. I don’t think I was the kid who was constantly running around or getting in trouble for not staying seated.

I could be forgetting some of it, but from what I remember, I wasn’t especially overly energetic compared with other kids. Is that the kind of thing you mean?
Do you often find yourself easily distracted by things going on around you, or by unrelated thoughts, even when you're trying to focus on a task?

Yeah… I think that does happen. I try not to let it show, especially in meetings, but I can get pulled off pretty easily.

Like, if I’m listening to a budget update, and someone’s phone vibrates, or there are people talking out in the hall, my attention just kind of goes there. Or sometimes it’s not even something outside — I’ll suddenly think of something I forgot to handle for the league, and then I realize I missed the next few minutes of what was being said.

It’s not like I’m trying to ignore people, but… yeah, I guess I do get distracted that way more than I’d like. Does that answer what you mean?

Would you say these attention and organization difficulties have caused real problems—like conflict, missed opportunities, or trouble keeping up—in your work, relationships, or other important areas of your life, not just occasional embarrassment?

I mean… I’m still functioning. I don’t want to make it sound like everything is falling apart, because it isn’t. I get by at work and I’m involved in things in the community.

But if I’m being honest, yes, it has caused some real problems. There have been times coworkers have had to kind of cover gaps for me, or a deadline slipped because I didn’t stay on top of something the way I should have. And I’ve definitely had to send those embarrassing last-minute apology messages to coworkers or friends when I forgot something or didn’t follow through when I meant to.

So… I guess it’s more than just being embarrassed once in a while. I don’t love admitting that, but yes.

Anxiety (F41.1) was considered given some mental 'checking' but this appears secondary to attentional lapses rather than a primary anxiety disorder; hyperkinetic conduct disorder (F90.1) was excluded due to absence of hyperactivity/impulsivity or conduct symptoms.
